units.title: Charges from the group
units: Where are the metals? Where are the nonmetals?
Group 17 gains 1 electron: charge 1−. The name ends in -ide.
Metal atoms lose 1, 2 or 3 valence electrons.
Nonmetal atoms gain electrons to reach eight.
A monatomic anion name ends in -ide.
B. Magnesium is in group 2. It loses 2 electrons.

units.title: The four to memorize
units: Fe 2+ and Fe 3+ , Cu + and Cu 2+ : two ions each.
The numeral is a version number, not a count.
Ag + and Zn 2+ have one ion each, so no numeral.
Rust and the iron ore hematite hold Fe 3+ .
Memory card: the six ions and their charges
Fe 2+ Fe 3+ Cu + Cu 2+ Ag + Zn 2+
Which metal needs a Roman numeral in its name?
C. Copper forms Cu + and Cu 2+ .

units.title: Balancing the charges
units: Every + stud needs a − socket. The total charge must be zero.
Ca 2+ has two studs, so it needs two Cl − ions. The charges 2+ and 2− add to zero.
Al 3+ and O 2− : how many of each ion make the total charge zero?
Two Al 3+ ions give a charge of 6+. Three O 2− ions give 6−. The total charge is zero.
The total charge of an ionic compound is zero. The formula shows the smallest whole-number ratio of ions.
C. Two Na + give 2+. One O 2− gives 2−.

units.title: Writing the formula
units: The small numbers count the ions.
Reduce to the lowest ratio: MgO, not Mg 2 O 2 .

units.title: The crisscross shortcut
units: Crisscross is a fast way to balance the charges.
Mg 2+ and O 2− : cross the charge numbers again.
Each charge number becomes the other ion's subscript. The signs drop.
Two Al 3+ ions give 6+. Three O 2− ions give 6−. The total charge is zero.
Crossing gives Mg 2 O 2 . Divide both counts by 2: MgO.
Crisscross is a shortcut, not the final formula. Always reduce the ratio, then check the total charge.
Crisscross gives Ca 2 O 2 . The formula is…
B. Reduce 2 : 2 to 1 : 1. The charges 2+ and 2− make zero.

units.title: Naming binary compounds
units: A name has two parts: the cation first, then the anion.
Name the cation first, then the anion root plus -ide. Common names omit prefixes because the ion charges determine the ratio.
B. The anion takes -ide. No prefix is needed.

units.title: The Stock system
units: Iron(II) and iron(III) are two different ions, like version numbers.
A different numeral gives a different formula: FeCl 3 and FeCl 2 .
Silver and zinc have one ion each. Their names have no numeral.
Start from the anion's charge. The metal must cancel it.
The copper ion's charge determines the formula. The Roman numeral records that charge in the name.
B. Two Cl − ions give 2−, so iron is 2+.

units.title: Polyatomic ions
units: Atom colors show the element, not the charge.
A polyatomic ion is a group of atoms with one shared charge.
An -ate ion contains oxygen. Nitrate is not nitride. Sulfate is not sulfide.
Nick the Camel ate Supper in Phoenix.
Consonants count O atoms. Vowels give the charge.
Sulfate, SO 4 2− : which statement is right?
A Each O is an oxide ion.
B It is the same as sulfide.
C. The charge belongs to the whole group.

units.title: Parentheses
units: OH − is one squad: one O and one H with one charge.
Two ammonium squads ride in parentheses. One sulfate squad needs none.
One nitrate squad, so no parentheses.
Treat a polyatomic ion as one unit. Never change the subscripts inside a polyatomic ion.
Write the formula of magnesium nitrate.
B. Mg 2+ needs two NO 3 − squads.

units.title: The two-way road
units: Work back: start from the anion. The copper ions must cancel its charge.
Name your formula again. Write your name again. Both must agree.
B. Three SO 4 2− give 6−. Two Fe share 6+, so each is 3+.

units: Write the formula of aluminum oxide from Al 3+ and O 2− . Explain why the ratio is correct.

Think alone. Do not talk yet.

The formula is Al 2 O 3 . Two aluminum ions provide 6+, and three oxide ions provide 6−. The total charge equals zero.

units.title: Checkpoint 2
units: Iron forms two different chlorides, FeCl 2 and FeCl 3 . Name both compounds and explain how you determined each Roman numeral.
Read the question. What is the anion?
Think alone. Do not talk yet.
Tell your partner your answer. Then listen.
Word bank: chloride is 1− total charge numeral = charge
the numeral is the iron charge?
FeCl 2 is iron(II) chloride. FeCl 3 is iron(III) chloride. Each chloride ion is 1−, so iron balances them.

units.title: Checkpoint 3
units: Some antacids contain aluminum hydroxide. Write its formula. Explain why it needs parentheses but NaOH does not.
Read the question. How many hydroxide ions does aluminum need?
Think alone. Do not talk yet.
Tell your partner your answer. Then listen.
Word bank: squad one charge three parentheses
The formula is Al(OH) 3 . Aluminum needs three hydroxide ions, so they go in parentheses. NaOH has one.
